name: p3-medium
text:
Summarise the following in three bullet points.

The DGX Spark is a compact workstation built around the GB10 Grace Blackwell superchip. It pairs an Arm CPU with a Blackwell GPU over a coherent link, sharing one pool of unified memory, so a model that is loaded once can be read by both sides without copies. The design trades peak bandwidth for capacity: a large mixture-of-experts model fits in memory whole, and each generated token only touches the experts the router selects. Engineers who write their own kernels for this chip have to think about launch overhead, about which memory is cached on the GPU side, and about how the host polls for completion. Small launches add up quickly when a layer needs many of them, so grouping work per layer matters more than raw arithmetic throughput. The practical outcome is that bandwidth per token, not compute, sets the speed of decoding, and that the fastest path keeps weights in the narrowest format the kernels can read directly.
